spec.full_target:
A sphere-valued map cannot vanish outside a compact set. As approved by
the user on 2026-10-23, interpret spatial compact support as compact support
of a perturbation from a **fixed unit vector**, locally uniformly in time.
This is a disclosed nontrivial interpretation, not a claimed author-issued
correction.

Let \(n,m\geq1\) be integers and let
\(u:\mathbb R^n\times(0,\infty)\to\mathbb R^m\) be jointly smooth.
Fix \(q\in\mathbb R^m\) with \(|q|=1\). Assume:

1. \(|u(x,t)|=1\) for all \(x\) and \(t>0\).
2. The acceleration \(u_{tt}-\Delta_xu\) is normal to the sphere at
   \(u\): at each point there is a real scalar \(a(x,t)\) with
   \(u_{tt}-\Delta_xu=a u\). No regularity of the selected scalar is
   assumed.
3. For every \(0<s<t<\infty\), a compact set
   \(C_{[s,t]}\subset\mathbb R^n\) exists such that \(u(x,r)=q\) for
   \(x\notin C_{[s,t]}\), \(r\in[s,t]\).

With Euclidean norms and Lebesgue measure, define

\[
e(x,t)=|u_t(x,t)|^2+\sum_{j=1}^n|\partial_{x_j}u(x,t)|^2,
\qquad E(t)=\int_{\mathbb R^n}e(x,t)\,dx.
\]

The spatial gradient square is the Frobenius square, and
\(\Delta_xu=\sum_j\partial_{x_jx_j}u\) component by component.
Prove integrability of \(e(\cdot,t)\), differentiability of \(E\),
and \(E'(t)=0\) for every \(t>0\). No assertion at time zero is required.
spec.conclusion: For every real t>0, e(·,t) is Lebesgue integrable on ℝⁿ, the finite energy E is differentiable at t, and E'(t)=0. Here e=|u_t|²+∑_{j=1}^n|∂_{x_j}u|² and E(t)=∫_{ℝⁿ}e(x,t) dx with Euclidean norms and Lebesgue measure; there is no assertion at time zero.

hypotheses.statement: u is jointly C∞ on ℝⁿ×(0,∞).
q∈ℝᵐ satisfies |q|=1 for the Euclidean norm.
For every x∈ℝⁿ and t>0, |u(x,t)|=1 for the Euclidean norm.
For every x∈ℝⁿ and t>0 there exists a real scalar a such that u_tt(x,t)−Δ_x u(x,t)=a u(x,t), with Δ_x u=∑_{j=1}^n ∂_{x_jx_j}u componentwise. No regularity or global choice of the scalar is assumed.
For every pair of real numbers 0<s<t<∞ there exists a compact C⊆ℝⁿ such that u(x,r)=q for every x∉C and every r∈[s,t].

definitions.definition: Space = Fin n → ℝ, the fixed standard coordinates on ℝⁿ, with its product norm, Borel structure and topology.
Value = Fin m → ℝ, the fixed standard coordinates on ℝᵐ, with its product norm and topology.
For v,w∈Value, dot(v,w)=∑_{k∈Fin m} v(k)w(k). This is the Euclidean dot product.
For v∈Value, normSq(v)=dot(v,v), the Euclidean norm squared.
In the fixed standard coordinates, ubar(x,t)=u(x,t) for t>0 and ubar(x,t)=q for t≤0. This is a total representative only; its definition asserts no regularity at t=0.

definitions.type: notation for calculus, topology and measure
definitions.definition: For maps between the stated normed spaces, Df and fderiv ℝ f denote the real Fréchet derivative (the total library operator, set to zero when no derivative exists); deriv f is the analogous one-variable real derivative. HasDerivAt f a t means f is differentiable at t with derivative a. ContDiffOn and ContDiffAt mean C^r regularity on a set and at a point, with ∞ meaning all finite orders and ω analytic. minSmoothness(κ,2) is 2 for real/complex normed fields and ω otherwise; IsSymmSndFDerivAt κ f p means D(Df)(p)(v)(w)=D(Df)(p)(w)(v) for all directions v,w. 𝓝 t is the neighborhood filter. support f={x:f(x)≠0}, tsupport f is its closure, and HasCompactSupport f means tsupport f is compact. ContinuousOn has its usual relative-set meaning. AEStronglyMeasurable means agreement almost everywhere with a strongly measurable function; Integrable means this measurability and finite integral of the norm, and IntegrableOn f C μ means Integrable f (μ restricted to C). The Bochner integral ∫ f dμ uses the library total convention; it is the ordinary finite Lebesgue integral when f is real and integrable. A set indicator equals its function on the set and zero off it. ae means outside a μ-null set. ‖c‖ₑ denotes the extended nonnegative norm used for ESeminormedAddMonoid; ordinary real numbers have finite extended norm. The standard structure names in source contracts carry their usual mathematical meanings (in particular OpensMeasurableSpace: open sets measurable; BorelSpace: measurable structure is Borel; IsFiniteMeasureOnCompacts: compact sets have finite measure; IsAddHaarMeasure: additive Haar measure).
V(x,t)_k=deriv (r↦ubar(x,r)_k) t, for each x,t and k∈Fin m.
L(x,t)=∑_{j∈Fin n} Ssp(j,x,t), the componentwise spatial Laplacian.

dx is canonical Lebesgue volume on Space: the product of the usual real Lebesgue measures in its fixed standard coordinates. It is the original dx on ℝⁿ. Spatial integrals without a displayed measure use dx.
e(x,t)=normSq(V(x,t))+∑_{j∈Fin n} normSq(Psp(j,x,t)). This is |u_t|²+∑_j |∂_{x_j}u|² at positive times, with the Euclidean/Frobenius squares and coefficient 1 on each term.
E(t)=∫_{Space} e(x,t) dx, using the total integral convention until integrability is proved. At positive times when integrable this is the original finite energy integral.

propositions.statement: The fixed standard-coordinate representation Space=Fin n→ℝ and Value=Fin m→ℝ identifies the original Euclidean map with ubar restricted to U; Euclidean squares are normSq and the original dx is the product Lebesgue volume dx with no scaling. At positive times V=u_t, A=u_tt, Psp(j)=∂_j u, Ssp(j)=∂_jj u, L=Δ_xu, e=|u_t|²+∑_j|∂_j u|² and E is the same total integral expression, finite whenever e is integrable. The fields ubar,V,A,Psp(j),Ssp(j),W(j),e,d are C∞ on U for every j∈Fin n. For every x∈Space, t>0, k∈Fin m and j∈Fin n: HasDerivAt (r↦ubar(x,r)_k) V(x,t)_k t; HasDerivAt (r↦V(x,r)_k) A(x,t)_k t; HasDerivAt (r↦Psp(j,x,r)_k) W(j,x,t)_k t; fderiv ℝ (y↦ubar(y,t)_k) x (basis(j))=Psp(j,x,t)_k; fderiv ℝ (y↦V(y,t)_k) x (basis(j))=W(j,x,t)_k; and fderiv ℝ (y↦Psp(j,y,t)_k) x (basis(j))=Ssp(j,x,t)_k. In particular the time derivative of Psp(j) and the spatial j derivative of V coincide. Moreover HasDerivAt (r↦e(x,r)) d(x,t) t, with d(x,t)=2 dot(V(x,t),A(x,t))+2∑_j dot(Psp(j,x,t),W(j,x,t)). No assertion of regularity across zero is made.

propositions.statement: For every t0>0 there exists a compact C⊆Space such that, writing J=[t0/2,3t0/2] and I=(t0/2,3t0/2), ubar(x,r)=q for all x∉C and r∈J. Every positive-order spacetime derivative of ubar vanishes on Cᶜ×I. In particular V,A,Psp(j),Ssp(j),W(j),e,d vanish there. For every r∈I and j∈Fin n,k∈Fin m, all scalar component spatial sections of V,A,Psp(j),Ssp(j),W(j), the sections e(·,r),d(·,r), and the products V_k A_k, Psp(j)_k W(j)_k, V_k Ssp(j)_k, V_k Psp(j)_k, W(j)_k Psp(j)_k at time r are continuous, have tsupport contained in C, and are dx-integrable. Their finite sums, dot products and finite real linear combinations are likewise continuous, compactly supported in C and integrable. In particular e(·,t) is dx-integrable for every t>0.

For each k∈Fin m the scalar products V_k Ssp(j)_k, W(j)_k Psp(j)_k and V_k Psp(j)_k at time t0, including the two directional-derivative products in the integration-by-parts application, are integrable.
propositions.origin: basis-proof.md:33–38; internal proof of class 3 B014.

propositions.statement: For every real t>0, e(·,t) is Lebesgue integrable on ℝⁿ, the finite energy E is differentiable at t, and E'(t)=0. Here e=|u_t|²+∑_{j=1}^n|∂_{x_j}u|² and E(t)=∫_{ℝⁿ}e(x,t) dx with Euclidean norms and Lebesgue measure; there is no assertion at time zero.

locals.declaration: Fix arbitrary target coordinate k∈Fin m.
Fix arbitrary spatial coordinate j∈Fin n.
Put p=(x,t), which lies in U.
Put Hess(v,w0)=D(Dw)(p)(v)(w0), the second Fréchet derivative evaluated in the indicated order.

argument.text: H001 fixes positive finite dimensions. Use the fixed standard coordinates on both original Euclidean spaces. For a vector in any such coordinate space, its maximum coordinate norm is at most its Euclidean norm, and its Euclidean norm is at most the square root of the number of coordinates times its maximum coordinate norm. Thus the coordinate identity and its inverse are continuous linear maps; they preserve Fréchet differentiability and all C∞ orders by the chain rule. The coordinates are the original standard ones, so dot and normSq are exactly the original dot product and squared Euclidean norm, not the product norm squared. Lebesgue measure in these standard coordinates is by definition the product of the usual real coordinate Lebesgue measures, giving dx with no Jacobian or rescaling. Restricting ubar to U recovers u, and conversely extension by q gives the total ubar. At a point of U a neighborhood stays in U, so all derivatives there are local and independent of the extension at nonpositive times. H002 therefore gives C∞ regularity of ubar on U. The derivative definitions, finite coordinate sums and the measure identification give the asserted meanings of V,A,Psp,Ssp,L,e,E once their actual derivative identities are checked below. Record F001: this coordinate representation, measure and norm identification is faithful, and ubar is C∞ on U.

produces.statement: The coordinate identities are continuous linear isomorphisms preserving the original Euclidean differential calculus; normSq is the Euclidean square and dx is the original Lebesgue measure. ubar restricted to U is u and ubar is C∞ on U. All derivatives at positive times are independent of the arbitrary extension.

argument.text: Fix arbitrary x,t>0,j,k as declared and put p=(x,t), w(y,r)=ubar(y,r)_k, T=(0,1), Xdir=(basis(j),0). F001 and continuous linear scalar projection give w C∞ on the open set U. Apply M006 over ℝ, with domain Space×ℝ, scalar codomain and both smoothness orders ∞: ∞+1=∞ supplies the order inequality, so Dw is C∞ on U. The derivative of the affine time injection r↦(x,r) sends h to (0,h); the derivative of y↦(y,t) sends h to (h,0). The ordinary chain rule identifies V(x,t)_k=Dw(p)T and Psp(j,x,t)_k=Dw(p)Xdir, first as HasDerivAt or HasFDerivAt assertions, then as equalities by uniqueness. These identities hold on all U, not just at p. Evaluation at a fixed direction is continuous linear, so the identities and smoothness of Dw show that V and every Psp(j) are C∞ on U, componentwise and hence as finite vector-valued maps. In particular the actual time derivative of each coordinate of ubar is V. Record F002 with these first-derivative and smoothness facts.

produces.statement: V and Psp(j0) are C∞ on U for every j0∈Fin n. For every x0∈Space,t1>0,k0∈Fin m, HasDerivAt (r↦ubar(x0,r)_k0) V(x0,t1)_k0 t1; the spatial derivative in direction basis(j0) is Psp(j0,x0,t1)_k0. At the chosen p, V(x,t)_k=Dw(p)T and Psp(j,x,t)_k=Dw(p)Xdir.

argument.text: Put Hess(v,w0)=D(Dw)(p)(v)(w0). Apply M006 again, this time to the C∞ map Dw with its continuous-linear-map codomain, and iterate for higher derivatives as needed; U is open and the ∞ order inequality remains valid. Differentiate the fixed evaluations from S002 by the chain rule. This gives ∂_t Psp(j,x,t)_k=Hess(T,Xdir), ∂_j V(x,t)_k=Hess(Xdir,T), A(x,t)_k=Hess(T,T), and Ssp(j,x,t)_k=Hess(Xdir,Xdir). F001 gives C² regularity of w at p because p∈U. Apply M005 over ℝ at order 2, where minSmoothness(ℝ,2)=2, to get Hess(T,Xdir)=Hess(Xdir,T). By the definition of W the common value is W(j,x,t)_k. The same derivative closure and fixed evaluations show A,Ssp(j),W(j) C∞ on U; this holds at every positive point and for every coordinate. Record F003: the full second-derivative regularity and the actual time derivative identities for V and Psp.

produces.statement: A, Ssp(j0), W(j0) are C∞ on U for every j0∈Fin n. For all x0∈Space,t1>0,k0∈Fin m,j0∈Fin n, HasDerivAt (r↦V(x0,r)_k0) A(x0,t1)_k0 t1 and HasDerivAt (r↦Psp(j0,x0,r)_k0) W(j0,x0,t1)_k0 t1. The spatial j0 derivative of V_k0 is W(j0)_k0 and the spatial j0 derivative of Psp(j0)_k0 is Ssp(j0)_k0.

argument.text: Apply M004 over ℝ to the time function V(x,·)_k multiplied by itself, using F003, to obtain derivative 2 V(x,t)_k A(x,t)_k for its square. Apply M004 also to Psp(j,x,·)_k multiplied by itself, using its time derivative W(j,x,t)_k from F003, to obtain 2 Psp(j,x,t)_k W(j,x,t)_k. The coordinate k and spatial index j are arbitrary; finite-sum differentiation therefore gives HasDerivAt (r↦e(x,r)) [2∑_k V(x,t)_k A(x,t)_k+2∑_j∑_k Psp(j,x,t)_k W(j,x,t)_k] t. Finite distributivity identifies the bracket with d(x,t). Smooth finite products and sums of F002 and F003 also show e and d are C∞ on U. Record F004: the displayed HasDerivAt identity with derivative d, and C∞ regularity of e,d.

produces.statement: e and d are C∞ on U, and for the arbitrary x and t>0, HasDerivAt (r↦e(x,r)) d(x,t) t.

argument.text: The spatial derivative identities for ubar, Psp and V are their definitions; F002 and F003 verify that they are genuine derivatives at positive times. Combining F001–F004 proves all regularity, mixed-derivative and energy-derivative clauses. Since x,t,j,k were arbitrary, close their quantifiers. The identified Laplacian is exactly L=∑_j Ssp(j), and the identified density and measure give the original total energy expression E without any change of coefficient. This proves N001.

applications.bindings: κ=ℝ, Z=Space×ℝ, Y0=ℝ, f=w, s=U, rOrder=sOrder=∞.
hypothesis_checks: The domain is a real finite product normed space and scalar codomain ℝ is a real normed space.
F001 and scalar projection give ContDiffOn ℝ ∞ w U.
U is the inverse image of the open positive ray under the continuous time projection.

applications.bindings: κ=ℝ, Z=Space×ℝ, Y0 the continuous-linear-map codomain of Dw and successively its derivative codomains, f=Dw and its successive derivatives, s=U, rOrder=sOrder=∞.
hypothesis_checks: Continuous linear maps between the specified normed spaces form the requisite real normed spaces.
S002 gives Dw smooth; repeated applications give the next smooth derivative before the following application.
U is open as established in S002.
At each application ∞+1=∞.

applications.bindings: κ=ℝ, Z=Space×ℝ, Y0=ℝ, f=w, point p=(x,t), rOrder=2; evaluate the conclusion at T and Xdir.
hypothesis_checks: These are real normed spaces.
F001 and scalar projection give C∞ on U; because p∈U and U is open, w is C² at p.
For the real field minSmoothness(ℝ,2)=2≤2.

applications.bindings: κ=Y0=ℝ; f=g=V(x,·)_k, a0=b0=A(x,t)_k, z=t, for each k.
hypothesis_checks: ℝ is a nontrivially normed field and a normed algebra over itself.
F003 gives the derivative of the first factor.
The identical second factor has the same derivative by F003.

applications.bindings: κ=Y0=ℝ; f=g=Psp(j,x,·)_k, a0=b0=W(j,x,t)_k, z=t, for each j,k.
hypothesis_checks: ℝ has the stated structures.
F003 supplies HasDerivAt for Psp(j,x,·)_k.
The second factor is the same function, so F003 applies again.

locals.declaration: Choose compact C with u=q on Cᶜ×[t0/2,3t0/2] by H006 at this slab.
The family consists of all scalar component sections of V,A,Psp(j),Ssp(j),W(j), and e,d, the five listed products in N002, and their finite sums, dot products and real linear combinations, at time r.
Take arbitrary h in this family.

argument.text: Fix arbitrary t0>0. The inequalities 0<t0/2<3t0/2 allow H006 to choose compact C such that u=q off C throughout J=[t0/2,3t0/2]. Put I=(t0/2,3t0/2). All times of J are positive, so the definition of ubar gives the same equality for ubar. In particular t0∈I. Record F001: C is compact and ubar=q on Cᶜ×J.

produces.statement: C is compact, t0∈I, and ubar(x1,r1)=q for all x1∉C and r1∈J.

argument.text: A compact subset C of the Hausdorff finite-dimensional space is closed. Thus O=Cᶜ×I is open. At each arbitrary p∈O the equality in F001 holds on a whole neighborhood: ubar is locally the constant q. Apply M007 to ubar and that constant on this neighborhood. The constant has zero derivative (its increments are zero), so D ubar(p)=0. This holds at every point of O. Reapply M007 to this derivative map and the zero map at every point of O; its derivative is again zero. Induction on the positive order now gives all iterated positive-order Fréchet derivatives zero on O: the first-order case is established; if the order-ℓ derivative map is zero throughout O, each point has a neighborhood on which that map is the constant zero, so M007 makes its next derivative zero there. The same chain-rule directional evaluations as in N001 identify V,A,Psp,Ssp,W with evaluations of the first two derivatives. Consequently V=A=Psp(j)=Ssp(j)=W(j)=0 on O for all j, and the formulas for e,d make both zero there. Record F002 with this universal vanishing conclusion.

produces.statement: Every positive-order spacetime derivative of ubar vanishes on O=Cᶜ×I. In particular V,A,Psp(j1),Ssp(j1),W(j1),e,d vanish there for every j1∈Fin n.

argument.text: Fix arbitrary r∈I and take the family of sections specified in the local declaration. By N001 each component section is continuous on the whole spatial space; e,d are continuous as well. Finite products, sums and dot products preserve continuity. F002 makes each of these sections zero off C. For an arbitrary section h in this family, support h⊆C. Since C is closed, its closure tsupport h is also contained in C; tsupport h is closed and hence a compact closed subset of the compact C. Apply M001 with domain Space, codomain ℝ and measure dx to h. This is a Borel real normed coordinate space; its Lebesgue measure is finite on compact sets. For example a compact set is contained in some finite coordinate box, whose product Lebesgue measure is finite, and monotonicity bounds the compact set's measure. Therefore the source gives dx-integrability of every such h. Record F003: all the stated sections at r have compact topological support contained in C and are integrable.

produces.statement: At the arbitrary r∈I, every h in family is continuous with tsupport h⊆C, has compact topological support, and is dx-integrable.

argument.text: The conclusions hold for every r∈I and every stated component, product, dot product and finite linear combination. Since t0∈I, this proves integrability of e(·,t0). The existence and vanishing conclusions depend only on the chosen slab and thus give the full existential statement N002 after closing the choice of C and the arbitrary t0. In particular every positive time has an integrable energy density. No vanishing assertion at the endpoints of J has been used.

applications.bindings: κ=ℝ, Z=Space×ℝ, Y0=Value; f1=ubar, f=the constant q, p arbitrary in O. Repeatedly take Y0 the iterated continuous-linear-map space, f1 the preceding derivative map and f the constant zero.
hypothesis_checks: The stated real normed spaces and their continuous-linear-map spaces provide the topological additive groups and real modules required by M007.
For the first application F001 and openness of O give equality on a neighborhood of each p; at every succeeding order the preceding step has established equality to zero throughout O.

applications.bindings: Z=Space, Y0=ℝ, μ=dx; f=h ranges over the displayed family of component sections, products, dot products and finite linear combinations at r∈I.
hypothesis_checks: Space has its Borel structure and dx is product Lebesgue measure finite on compact sets; scalar codomain ℝ is a normed additive commutative group, as explained in S003.
N001 gives continuous component sections, and the finite products and sums defining h preserve continuity.
F002 gives vanishing off closed compact C, so S003 proves tsupport h⊆C and compactness of tsupport h before invoking M001.

locals.declaration: Choose C from N002 for t0, with all support and integrability conclusions there.
Choose B0 with |d(x,r)|≤B0 on Kprod from F001.
Put bnd(x)=B if x∈C, and bnd(x)=0 otherwise.

argument.text: Fix t0>0 and choose C from N002 with its full conclusions. Put I=(t0/2,3t0/2), eta=t0/4>0, Ktime=[t0−eta,t0+eta], stime=(t0−eta,t0+eta). Explicitly t0−eta=3t0/4>t0/2 and t0+eta=5t0/4<3t0/2. Thus Ktime⊂I⊂(0,∞), and stime is an open neighborhood of t0. N002 supplies vanishing of d off C for all these times, and integrability and continuity of the spatial sections e,d throughout I.

Set Kprod=C×Ktime. Compactness of C from N002 and compactness of the closed bounded real interval Ktime show that Kprod is compact. It lies in U. N001 makes d continuous on U, so its restriction is continuous on Kprod. Apply M008 to d on Kprod to obtain a real bound for |d|. Record F001: there exists a real bound on Kprod. This existence assertion is valid also for empty C.

produces.statement: There exists a real c0 such that |d(x1,r1)|≤c0 for every (x1,r1)∈Kprod.

argument.text: Choose B0 from F001 and put B=max(B0,0), bnd=B·1_C. The compact subset C of the Hausdorff coordinate space is closed and hence Borel measurable. Its Lebesgue measure is finite: compactness bounds it in a finite coordinate box and dx of that box is the finite product of its side lengths. The real number B has finite extended norm. M009, with scalar value B and set C, gives IntegrableOn (constant B) C dx. M010, using measurability of C, turns this into Integrable bnd dx. Thus record F002: bnd is an integrable nonnegative bound, and |d(x,r)|≤B on C×Ktime.

produces.statement: bnd is dx-integrable, B≥0, and |d(x1,r1)|≤B whenever (x1,r1)∈C×Ktime; bnd=B on C and zero off C.

argument.text: For each spatial x and every r∈stime, if x∈C the compact bound in F002 gives |d(x,r)|≤B=bnd(x); if x∉C, N002 gives d(x,r)=0 and bnd(x)=0. Consequently the entire predicate ∀ r∈stime, |d(x,r)|≤bnd(x) holds for every x, and hence for dx-almost every x with a single, empty exceptional set. Separately N001 gives HasDerivAt (s↦e(x,s)) d(x,r) r for every x and every r∈stime, because all these times are positive. Thus this universal-in-r predicate also holds for dx-almost every x. N001 gives continuity of e(·,r) for r∈stime and of d(·,t0); continuous real functions on the Borel coordinate space are strongly measurable and hence ae strongly measurable. This supplies eventual measurability of e because stime is a neighborhood. N002 gives integrability of e(·,t0). Record F003 with these premises, preserving the ae-first order in both quantified hypotheses.

produces.statement: stime∈𝓝 t0. Eventually r→t0, e(·,r) is dx-ae strongly measurable; e(·,t0) is dx-integrable; d(·,t0) is dx-ae strongly measurable. For dx-almost every x1, for every r1∈stime, |d(x1,r1)|≤bnd(x1). For dx-almost every x1, for every r1∈stime, HasDerivAt (s↦e(x1,s)) d(x1,r1) r1. Each of the two ae assertions follows from its corresponding everywhere-in-space assertion.

argument.text: Apply M002 with α=Space, μ=dx, real parameter and codomain, F(r,x)=e(x,r), F'(r,x)=d(x,r), basepoint t0, neighborhood stime and bound bnd. F003 gives its neighborhood, eventual measurability, base integrability, derivative-section measurability, ae-first bound and ae-first derivative premises. F002 gives integrability of the bound. M002 concludes Integrable d(·,t0) and HasDerivAt (r↦∫ e(x,r) dx) (∫ d(x,t0) dx) t0. By the definition of E this is the desired derivative statement for the actual energy integral. N002 ensures that the integrals e defining E are finite at all positive times, so this is differentiability of the requested finite function.

The bound, compact set and time neighborhood were allowed to depend on the arbitrary t0>0. Eliminate their local choices and close the quantifier on t0 in F004. This proves N003; no bound over the whole half-space or assertion at zero has been added.

hypothesis_checks: The coordinate product is topological and ℝ is a seminormed additive group.
C is compact by N002; Ktime is a closed bounded real interval; their product is compact.
N001 makes d smooth on U, hence continuous on the subset Kprod⊂U.
Space is measurable, dx is its Lebesgue measure and ℝ carries its usual topological ESeminormedAddMonoid structure.
The compact set C has finite dx-measure, as proved by the finite-box bound in S003.
B is real, so its extended norm is finite.

applications.bindings: α=Space, μ=dx, s=C, Y0=ℝ, f=the constant B; the indicator is bnd.
hypothesis_checks: Space,dx and ℝ have the requisite structures, as for M009.
Compact C is closed in the Hausdorff coordinate space, hence Borel measurable.

applications.bindings: α=Space, μ=dx, κ=ℝ, Y0=ℝ, b=bnd, F(r,x)=e(x,r), F'(r,x)=d(x,r), z0=t0, s=stime.
hypothesis_checks: Space has its Borel measurable structure; dx is Lebesgue; parameter and codomain ℝ have all stated normed structures.
S001 and F003 give stime∈𝓝 t0.
F003 proves ae strong measurability for every time in the neighborhood stime, hence eventually.
N002 and F003 give integrability of e(·,t0).
F003 gives continuity and thus ae strong measurability of d(·,t0).
F003 proves ∀ᵐ x, ∀ r∈stime, |d(x,r)|≤bnd(x), from the same everywhere-in-x predicate; real norm is absolute value.
F002 gives Integrable bnd dx.
F003 gives ∀ᵐ x, ∀ r∈stime, HasDerivAt (s↦e(x,s)) d(x,r) r, from an everywhere-in-x predicate, using N001 and stime⊂(0,∞).

locals.declaration: Use an arbitrary coordinate k∈Fin m in the component derivative calculation.
Choose a scalar a0 at the current point with A(x,t)−L(x,t)=a0 ubar(x,t), from H005 and the correspondence in N001.

argument.text: Fix arbitrary x and t>0. H004 and the coordinate identification in N001 give ∑_k ubar(x,r)_k²=1 for every r>0, hence on a neighborhood of t. For arbitrary k apply M004 over ℝ to ubar(x,·)_k multiplied by itself; N001 supplies its actual derivative V(x,t)_k. The square has derivative 2 ubar(x,t)_k V(x,t)_k. Differentiating the finite sum gives derivative 2 dot(ubar(x,t),V(x,t)). Since the sum agrees locally with the constant 1, its derivative is zero by locality and uniqueness of derivatives. Division by 2 yields dot(ubar,V)=0; commutativity of real multiplication yields dot(V,ubar)=0. Record F001: these two tangency identities at (x,t).

At this point take just the scalar witness a0 from H005. N001 identifies the original u_tt and Δ_xu with A and L, and u with ubar, so A(x,t)−L(x,t)=a0 ubar(x,t). By finite distributivity of dot and F001, dot(V,A−L)=dot(V,a0 ubar)=a0 dot(V,ubar)=0. Record F002: the required normality cancellation at (x,t). This uses no function selecting scalar witnesses and no derivative of the witness.

Both identities are independent of the chosen scalar's identity. Eliminate that existential choice and universally quantify the arbitrary x and positive t. F001 and F002 prove N004. The optional explicit scalar formula and twice-differentiated unit constraint from the original proof are not needed by this authorized route.

applications.bindings: κ=Y0=ℝ, f=g=(r↦ubar(x,r)_k), a0=b0=V(x,t)_k, z=t, for each k.
hypothesis_checks: Real scalars have the required field and algebra structures.
N001 gives HasDerivAt (r↦ubar(x,r)_k) V(x,t)_k t.
The second factor is the same function and has the same derivative from N001.

argument.text: Fix arbitrary t0>0,j∈Fin n,k∈Fin m. On the entire spatial space set f(x)=V(x,t0)_k, g(x)=Psp(j,x,t0)_k and v=basis(j). N001 gives their C∞ regularity as spatial sections: the affine inclusion x↦(x,t0) stays in U and smoothness is local at each point. Thus f and g are differentiable everywhere, in particular on the respective topological supports of g and f. The actual directional derivatives from N001 are Df(x)v=W(j,x,t0)_k and Dg(x)v=Ssp(j,x,t0)_k. By N002 at time t0, all three products (Df v)g, f(Dg v) and fg are continuous with compact support and integrable: they are W(j)_k Psp(j)_k, V_k Ssp(j)_k and V_k Psp(j)_k. Record F001 with these derivative and applicability facts.

produces.statement: f,g are differentiable everywhere on Space; for every x1∈Space, Df(x1)v=W(j,x1,t0)_k and Dg(x1)v=Ssp(j,x1,t0)_k. The three products (Df v)g, f(Dg v), fg are dx-integrable.

argument.text: Apply M003 on the finite-dimensional real space Space with its Borel structure, canonical Lebesgue additive Haar measure dx, scalar field ℝ, functions f,g and direction v. The hypotheses are F001. The conclusion is exactly ∫ V(x,t0)_k Ssp(j,x,t0)_k dx = −∫ W(j,x,t0)_k Psp(j,x,t0)_k dx. Record this scalar identity as F002.

produces.statement: ∫_{Space} V(x1,t0)_k Ssp(j,x1,t0)_k dx1 = −∫_{Space} W(j,x1,t0)_k Psp(j,x1,t0)_k dx1.

argument.text: Because k was arbitrary, F002 holds for every k∈Fin m. Sum these finitely many identities. N002 supplies integrability of each summand, so finite-sum linearity commutes integral and sum. Expanding dot gives ∫ dot(V,Ssp(j)) = −∫ dot(W(j),Psp(j)). Real multiplication commutes in each coordinate, hence dot(W(j),Psp(j))=dot(Psp(j),W(j)). Negating and rearranging gives ∫ dot(Psp(j),W(j)) = −∫ dot(V,Ssp(j)). Both integrands are integrable by N002, as are all the auxiliary products already checked. Record F003: the integration-by-parts identity at t0,j, including those integrability assertions.

produces.statement: At t0,j, ∫ dot(Psp(j,x1,t0),W(j,x1,t0)) dx1 = −∫ dot(V(x1,t0),Ssp(j,x1,t0)) dx1. Both integrands are integrable, and each of V_k1 Ssp(j)_k1, W(j)_k1 Psp(j)_k1 and V_k1 Psp(j)_k1 at this time is integrable for every k1∈Fin m.

argument.text: Close the arbitrary j and positive t0 in F003. This is precisely N005, with the whole-space integration-by-parts identity required for the final energy calculation.

applications.bindings: Z=Space, μ=dx, κ=ℝ, v=basis(j), f(x)=V(x,t0)_k, g(x)=Psp(j,x,t0)_k.
hypothesis_checks: Space is a finite-dimensional real normed space with Borel structure; dx is its canonical Lebesgue additive Haar measure; ℝ is a normed field and real normed algebra.
F001 identifies (Df v)g with W(j)_k Psp(j)_k, integrable by N002.
F001 identifies f(Dg v) with V_k Ssp(j)_k, integrable by N002.
F001 identifies fg with V_k Psp(j)_k, integrable by N002.
F001 proves f differentiable everywhere, hence on tsupport g.
F001 proves g differentiable everywhere, hence on tsupport f.

argument.text: Fix arbitrary t0>0. N002 gives integrability of e(·,t0), d(·,t0), each component product V_k A_k, Psp(j)_k W(j)_k and V_k Ssp(j)_k, and their dot products and finite linear combinations. Thus every integral in the following finite calculation is well-defined and finite. N003 gives HasDerivAt E (∫ d(x,t0) dx) t0. Record F001 with this derivative statement and the integrability facts just listed.

produces.statement: HasDerivAt E (∫ d(x1,t0) dx1) t0; e(·,t0), d(·,t0), dot(V,A), every dot(Psp(j1),W(j1)), every dot(V,Ssp(j1)), and their finite real linear combinations at t0 are dx-integrable.

argument.text:
Use F001 to distribute finite sums and real scalar factors through integrals, the definition of d, N005 for each j, and L=∑_j Ssp(j). All integrands here are evaluated at (x,t0):
∫ d = 2∫ dot(V,A) + 2∑_j ∫ dot(Psp(j),W(j))
     = 2∫ dot(V,A) − 2∑_j ∫ dot(V,Ssp(j))
     = 2∫ dot(V,A−∑_j Ssp(j))
     = 2∫ dot(V,A−L) = 0.
The penultimate algebra uses finite distributivity of dot and the integral's linearity for the integrable terms in F001. The last equality follows from the pointwise cancellation N004 at every x and positive t0, followed by the integral of the zero function. Hence the derivative value in F001 is zero. Record F002: HasDerivAt E 0 t0.

HasDerivAt E 0 t0 in F002 implies differentiability at t0 and E'(t0)=0 by the definition and uniqueness of the derivative. N002 already gives integrability of e(·,t0), so E(t0) is the actual finite energy, not a value assigned by the total integral convention. N001 identifies every derivative, Euclidean square, Frobenius finite sum and the measure with the original target. Thus the original density has coefficient 1 on |u_t|² and on each spatial derivative square, and the original E is differentiable with derivative zero at every positive time. Close the arbitrary t0 to obtain P, including integrability. No assertion at time zero is made.
